body:
For the first point this is entirely part of `PopupMenu`, but adding an option (off by default, to preserve compatibility) to check and unckeck on click would be pretty simple, but it should remain optional so you can prevent it if needed, etc.

For the second we could proxy some of the options from `PopupMenu` as properties on `MenuButton` to make it easier to use, that could be fragile though as it requires keeping the two in sync

For the third point that's harder to communicate in the editor, but the documentation clarifies this

The third could be addressed by doing either of these things: 1) Renaming Items to Popup Items 2) Adding PopupMenu Property pointing to the PopupMenu of the MenuButton that contains these properties (best option IMO) the 2nd option would also allow for resolving the 2nd issue, as it would also contain the hide_on_checkable_item_selection option as well as other PopupMenu options
The second would require a whole new system in the inspector, we can't use raw objects that way except by adding a custom plugin

Please stay constructive and keep terms like "horrible" or "hot mess" out of UX feedback. This is really not conducive to contributors wanting to evaluate your feedback when it's delivered in this manner.

This is not a platform to vent out but to contribute to making Godot better, with respect for everyone involved.

The only alternatives I could come put with are "Unusable" instead of "Horrible" which is not fitting as technically it is usable, you just need to know what you're doing. If you've got something that better Describes the issue without being technically inaccurate or too verbose, I'm all Ears. As for the other complaint... "Hot mess" definition states that it is "A thing that is spectacularly unsuccessful or disordered" which the MenuButton most definitely fits, as it is unsuccessful at providing what is expected of it, and it is also disordered in the fact it actively does things you don't expect it to do by default, and it doesn't expose itself in the manner the user expects based on the rest of the user experience with the Engine, causing confusion and yes some level of frustration (as is the case really when you hit any kind of an issue, and this I've worked out in half an hour, but for more novice users could easily take days of fruitless work trying to figure it out and potentially fail at figuring it out even partially). I stand by this choice, for it's perfectly descriptive and informative of it's state and the reasons for that are immediately stated/argumented explaining exactly why it is so thus removing any ambiguity the statement has on it's own. Without using that term I'd have needed to write a whole wall of text that's basically just the Definition of the term "Hot mess" which would needlessly 1) Waste my time writing additional Text 2) Waste the readers time reading the additional Text 3) Naturally increase the Risk losing Focus (by increasing the quantity of text to parse) for both the reader and author (in this case me), reducing the Quality of Communication, or requiring even further Editing and Formatting to help the Reader, at the expense of More of my time writing this P.S. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111985#issuecomment-3442099022 and this comment should be marked off-topic, as they don't have anything actually related to the issue, and are merely related to the language used in the issue report. Also while I understand that stand alone these words (especially "horrible") have negative connotations, please first consider the 2nd expectation of https://godotengine.org/code-of-conduct/ and first read through the literal meanings of the words used to see if what is said makes sense before jumping to the connotations of words to try to make sense of it.
